headline: Last session: Sensex crashed over 1,200 points as crude oil spikes and geopolitical tensions weighed on markets

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Tuesday, 29 September.

why: Crude oil price spikes and geopolitical developments weighed heavily on market sentiment (Articles 7, 13, 17).
Proposed insurance curbs contributed to selling pressure in Indian shares (Article 17).
Rising US yields and global macroeconomic triggers kept investors cautious (Articles 13, 16).
A 3-day nationwide bank strike starting September 28 raised concerns over banking service disruptions (Article 3).
whatHappening: In the last trading session, Sensex fell over 1,200 points to hit 3-month lows while Nifty broke below 23,100 (Articles 14, 15).
Trans ACNR Solutions and eight other companies filed IPO draft papers with SEBI (Article 8).
Petronet LNG announced a decision to pay 1% of its profit as commission to directors (Article 5).
Indian Navy Chief invited Skyroot to build space capabilities for the armed forces (Article 4).
summary: Indian stock markets remain closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Tuesday, 29 September. In the last trading session, Sensex crashed over 1,200 points and Nifty dropped below 23,100 due to rising crude oil prices and geopolitical tensions. Key focus areas for the week ahead include global cues, crude oil movements, and a 3-day nationwide bank strike.
